sam: Heads-up — after the v2.14.3 runtime canary rollout at ~09:10 UTC I'm seeing a big p99 jump for text-generation routes. p50 unchanged, p95 +12%, p99 +80%. Canaries are ~10% of traffic.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: runtime/v2.14.3 -> canary pool (09:10 UTC) :rocket:

ali: Looking at traces — latency concentrated on the hot-path `generateToken` call. Queueing time on the request queue spiked on three canary hosts. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/latency/route-gen (short link)

mira: Any recent changes in kernel selection or batcher heuristics in this rollout? I remember a refactor to selector logic landed in the runtime two commits ago. Could be causing heavier tail for some sequence lengths. :thinking:

joe: I can repro locally with a long-context load pattern. Quick repro: 
```
# run k6 script to hammer long-context generation
k6 run --vus 30 --duration 3m scripts/long_context_gen.js --env API_KEY=REDACTED
```
I saw similar p99 tail locally when sequence length > 2048 and the hotpath config flips to the new kernel.

sam: Good. Hypothesis: `select_kernel_v2` (new selector) picks a slower kernel for some shard sizes causing queueing and stalled token emission. Immediate mitigations: 1) force legacy kernel on canary hosts, 2) disable batcher micro-optimizations, or 3) rollback canary.

ali: I'm trying mitigation (1) now: SSHed into two canary hosts and set `RUNTIME_KERNEL=legacy` env, restarted runtime process on those nodes (rolling restart). Will monitor p99.

oncall: Also toggled `BATCHER_OPTIMIZATIONS=false` on the canary auto-scaling group as a quick test. Initial after-30s metric: p99 down ~28% on those hosts. Keeping that change while we bisect.

mira: For the bisect plan: bisect commits between v2.14.2 and v2.14.3 in the runtime repo. Focus on the kernel selector refactor and any batching changes. Steps: 
1) run unit/perf test for `selector` on the CI harness with sequence-length heavy workloads
2) promote candidate commits to an isolated canary with 1 node and targeted traffic 
3) collect full traces and `trace-id` examples for failed requests

sam: I'll open an infra ticket with the three affected host IDs and attach heap/trace logs. Also adding a guard: update routing policy to prefer legacy model variants for enterprise customers until we have a fix.

al i: (typo) ack :thumbsup:

joe: If we need a rollback, recommended command: `rw rollout rollback --component runtime --to v2.14.2 --scope canary` — that rolls canary back first without touching prod pool. Pre-checks: drained connections and warm cache.

oncall: Note: disabling batcher opt reduced p99 but increased per-token CPU on canary hosts ~5%. Cost trade-off but acceptable short-term.

sam: Summary / next actions: 
- Keep batcher optimizations disabled on canary (oncall)
- ali to finish forcing legacy kernel on remaining canary hosts and report p99 trend (in 5m)
- mira & joe to start commit bisect and run CI perf tests focused on selector/batcher diffs
- sam to create infra ticket with traces/logs and set rollback playbook ready if p99 doesn't stabilize in 15m

sam: Thanks team — please post quick status updates here.

ali: p99 improving after legacy kernel on 2/3 hosts, rolling restart on last host now.

mira: started bisect — first suspect commit hash `a1b2c3d` touches selector thresholds. Pushing perf job now.

joe: perf job shows regression reproduces with `a1b2c3d` when seq_len > 2048. Capturing traces and attaching to the ticket.

sam: Excellent. If bisect confirms, plan patch + canary fix and then controlled rollout.

oncall: posted interim note to incidents channel and paged oncall rotation.

sam: :thumbsup:
